name: Human factors pre-check framework v0
purpose: Questions a reviewer asks of an alert, a note or an order set, written as a design-level list of failure modes (a one-pass FMEA style view). Pre-check only. Not a medical device.

alert_inputs.note: Alert criteria are judged for one audience at one timing. Both lists are practice, not evidence, until a source is added.

criteria.question: Does the alert name the value or the reason that matters?
criteria.failure_mode: The reader cannot tell why it fired, so it is dismissed by habit and a real warning is missed.
criteria.source: wiki/Human Factors in Clinical Information Design

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer reads the text and finds only generic words such as 'caution' or 'check'.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Can this alert be told apart from the other alerts on the same screen?
criteria.failure_mode: Alerts of different weight look the same, so the serious one is treated like the minor ones.
criteria.source: wiki/Human Factors in Clinical Information Design

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer lays the alerts side by side and cannot tell two types apart at a glance.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does the alert offer more than a dismiss button, such as a choice or a reason?
criteria.failure_mode: The user can only close the alert, so safe action and override look the same.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Button labels are only X, OK or Cancel.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does the alert name the next action, and does each button match that action?
criteria.failure_mode: The reader sees a problem but not what to do, so the next step is guessed.
criteria.source: wiki/Human Factors in Clinical Information Design

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer asks 'what do I do now?' and the alert does not answer.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Is the alert meant for the role that can act on it (the audience input)?
criteria.failure_mode: The wrong person gets the alert, so it is ignored, or the right person never sees it.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer cannot name who must act on the alert.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does the alert appear at a step where the action is still possible (the timing input)?
criteria.failure_mode: The alert comes too early or too late to change the outcome, and adds to alert fatigue.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer finds the alert shows after the step it concerns.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: If the alert shows an error, does it say what went wrong and how to fix it?
criteria.failure_mode: The user repeats the same failing step and loses time.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Error text has no instruction word.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Can the alert be closed or undone without a forced choice?
criteria.failure_mode: The user is trapped in the alert and picks any option to move on.

fmea_fields.early_sign: No close, cancel or undo control is found on the alert box.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are the alert buttons at least 24 x 24 CSS px?
criteria.failure_mode: The wrong button is pressed and a warning is overridden by mistake.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Measured button box is under 24 x 24 CSS px.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Is the alert text readable against its background (contrast at least 4.5 to 1)?
criteria.failure_mode: Text is missed in a bright ward or on a poor screen.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Contrast ratio from the screenshot is under 4.5 to 1.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Is the note split into fields or headings, not one long block of free text?
criteria.failure_mode: The reader skims a wall of text and misses the one fact that matters.
criteria.source: wiki/Human Factors in Clinical Information Design

fmea_fields.early_sign: Text length is long and no heading or field label is found.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are the standard handover fields all present?
criteria.failure_mode: A field is left out, so the next shift does not know a key fact.
criteria.source: wiki/Human Factors in Clinical Information Design

fmea_fields.early_sign: A field from the handover structure is missing.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are open tasks ranked by risk or by time?
criteria.failure_mode: A time-critical task is buried below routine ones and done late.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer finds tasks in the order they were written, not the order they matter.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does the note avoid abbreviations that can be misread (for example 'U' for units)?
criteria.failure_mode: A misread abbreviation is copied into an order and a wrong dose is given.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Text pattern finds a listed abbreviation.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are error-prone abbreviations kept out of the order set text?
criteria.failure_mode: A misread abbreviation leads to a wrong dose or wrong frequency across many patients.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Text pattern finds a listed abbreviation in an order line.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Do look-alike drug names show tall-man letters in the pick list?
criteria.failure_mode: A look-alike name is picked by mistake and the wrong drug is ordered.

fmea_fields.early_sign: A name from the look-alike pair list appears without tall-man letters.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are the controls in the order set at least 24 x 24 CSS px?
criteria.failure_mode: The wrong box is ticked, and the error repeats across the set.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Measured control box is under 24 x 24 CSS px.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does each action have its own label, with no label used for two actions?
criteria.failure_mode: The user cannot tell which action a button will start.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Same label text found on two controls with different effects.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are the items that are pre-ticked a safe default?
criteria.failure_mode: A pre-ticked item is accepted without thought and given to a patient it does not suit.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer finds a pre-ticked item that is not right for every patient.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Does the set say what it is for and who may use it?
criteria.failure_mode: The set is used for the wrong patient group.

fmea_fields.early_sign: No purpose line or user group is found at the top of the set.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score

criteria.question: Are there items in the set that repeat or conflict with each other?
criteria.failure_mode: Two orders overlap and the patient gets a double dose.

fmea_fields.early_sign: Reviewer finds two items with the same drug or class.
fmea_fields.label: guess, not a score
